passages.provision_quote: On conviction of an offense under this article, the judge shall enter an order that requires the person to return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin.
passages.note: Senate-engrossed text of the measure he voted for; it also states "This section may only be enforced prospectively." and names no voter.
Bill history page for the same instrument; it prints the Senate tally but names no member and prints no provision.

rows.reasoning: Shope voted Y on HCR2060 (2024), a referral whose illegal-entry article orders a convicted person to "return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin", and which "may only be enforced prospectively". That puts him on the enforcement side but matches no rung's clauses: the removal reaches only persons convicted of unlawful entry after the act takes effect, so it is not "Deport all undocumented immigrants, starting with those who have criminal records". It also never says long-settled immigrants should be left in place — the prospective-only limit is silence about them, not the clause "while leaving long-settled undocumented immigrants in place" (V4.2 "Silence is not a clause").
needs_source: Shope's own words or a further record stating whom Arizona should remove beyond new unlawful entrants, to separate "Focus deportation on recent arrivals while leaving long-settled undocumented immigrants in place" from "Deport all undocumented immigrants, starting with those who have criminal records"
